review_basis: Final top-down PNG after deterministic validation round 1

review_items.concrete_reason: The south-center door opens into an unoccupied central turn-in field. cabinet_files_south_east is east of its clearance, chair_work_east is far north of it, and floor_lamp_window_reading is confined to the west reading pocket.

The rendered targets for desk_work_east, cabinet_files_south_east, bookcase_reference_north, and armchair_window_reading are all reachable from the door. The open middle acts as a branching field rather than a narrow corridor between furniture.

chair_work_east has a west-side pull-out zone away from the door, desk_work_east has a seated work zone, bookcase_reference_north has a south-side browsing zone, cabinet_files_south_east has a north-side operating zone, and armchair_window_reading retains its diagonal approach zone.

desk_work_east and chair_work_east are a single focused work pair. armchair_window_reading, side_table_window_reading, and floor_lamp_window_reading form a separate brief-reading group, with neither group using the other's operating clearance.

The bulky bookcase, cabinet, and desk are kept to three different walls. armchair_window_reading is set inward below the window, so the center and the entire south entry strip remain intentionally open rather than being filled with auxiliary furniture.

The desk is given an open room-facing work position, the bookcase presents its accessible side toward the aisle, and the file cabinet is close to but not inside the desk-chair area. The armchair is near natural light without blocking the window.

desk_work_east faces west with chair_work_east facing it from the west; bookcase_reference_north presents south into the room; cabinet_files_south_east presents north to its service field; and armchair_window_reading is diagonally directed toward its open south-east approach rather than directly at a wall.

desk_work_east is the primary functional anchor. bookcase_reference_north and cabinet_files_south_east are boundary storage support, while the smaller armchair group is intentionally secondary and visually separated on the west side.

The closest home_office_authored_001 puts its desk on the north-east, bookcase on the west, cabinet on the east, and reading chair in the south-west. This scene instead uses an east-wall desk, north bookcase, south file cabinet, and north-west window reading group; the 0.4 wall-attachment similarity, 0.319954 normalized position RMS, and 0.166667 yaw similarity confirm it is not a simple mirror or asset substitution.
